== Biography ==

The Queen, commonly referred to as the Queen of Hearts, is a ruler in Wonderland. She reigns alongside the King and is distinguished primarily by her violent temperament and immediate resort to capital punishment.

Her propensity for threats of execution is demonstrated repeatedly throughout her interactions. When a Hatter performed a song at a tea gathering, she rose abruptly and shouted, "He's murdering the time! Off with his head!" During a croquet match, she entered such a furious state that she repeatedly stamped about and shouted "Off with his head!" or "Off with her head!" at approximately one-minute intervals. The frequency and apparent arbitrariness of her execution orders suggest that such sentences are routine in her court; observers have remarked upon the remarkable fact that anyone survives in her domain at all.

The Queen maintains an active presence in her court's daily life. She participates directly in recreational activities such as croquet, in which she employs hedgehogs as equipment. When she encounters newcomers in formal processions, she questions them directly and with severity. When individuals such as the Knave of Hearts fail to meet her expectations, she expresses her displeasure sharply, dismissing them with contempt. Her shrill voice is most commonly heard issuing orders for the execution of those who have incurred her displeasure.

== Narrative role ==

The Queen invites guests to a croquet game, extending invitations through footmen. The Hatter had earlier quarreled with Time itself, having been accused by the Queen of murdering time and threatened with execution.

At the croquet game, the Queen's true character emerges. She falls into a furious passion, stamping about and repeatedly shouting demands for beheading—approximately once per minute. Her arbitrary execution sentences for minor infractions transform the game from sport into an exercise in chaos and terror, with players quarreling, fighting, and scrambling in fear.

Alice encounters the Queen's magnificence directly when the Queen's procession passes. Alice deliberately refuses to bow to the Queen, an act of insolence that nearly provokes the Queen to execute her. The King intervenes, reminding the Queen that Alice is merely a child, and thus spares her from death. Undeterred, the Queen continues sentencing numerous players to execution as the croquet game proceeds.

Yet the Gryphon later reveals to Alice that the Queen's threats are empty—no one actually dies from her sentences. The Queen demonstrates her impulsive cruelty further by suddenly appearing and threatening the Duchess with execution, causing the Duchess to flee in fear. Finally, the Queen presides over the trial of the Knave of Hearts, who stands accused of stealing the Queen's tarts.

== Personality ==

The Queen is volatile and uses execution as her default response to displeasure. When the Hatter begins singing during a tea party, she jumps up at once and shouts "He's murdering the time! Off with his head!" — condemning him to death for a musical performance. During croquet, she descends into "a furious passion," stamping about the ground and shouting execution orders at rapid intervals, repeating "Off with his head!" or "Off with her head!" about once every minute.

Her authority is absolute and entirely unquestioned. She orders even her guests to execution during her own entertainments, and her subjects exist in constant, justified fear of her judgment. Alice observes that execution is employed so casually in her realm that the mere survival of anyone is a matter of wonder. Her voice is shrill and penetrating, sharp enough to cut through the chaos she herself creates.

When displeased, the Queen dismisses subordinates with contempt—calling the Knave of Hearts an "Idiot!" and tossing her head impatiently. She addresses those who come before her with severity and shows little interest in their responses. Her manner is dismissive and commanding, brooking no disagreement or hesitation.

The Queen rules through terror alone, displaying no mercy or reconsideration in her condemnations. She is arbitrary and capricious—her favor unpredictable, her wrath absolute, and her judgment final. To all in her realm, she appears as an embodiment of pure, unmitigated danger.

== Relationships ==

'''[[King]]''' — family. The King and Queen of Hearts are seated together on their throne, seemingly ruling jointly. The King appears to show restraint toward the Queen's violent impulses, urging her to consider that Alice is only a child.

'''[[Alice]]''' — enemy. Alice appears to have crossed the Queen, speaking boldly in her presence. The Queen is notably silent in response to Alice's defiance.

'''[[Duchess]]''' — enemy. The Queen orders the Duchess to be brought to her from prison, suggesting tension between them.

'''[[Knave]]''' — employment. The Knave seems to serve the Queen, obeying her commands carefully during formal proceedings.

'''[[Bill]]''' — enemy. The Queen's volatile temperament seems to pose a threat to inhabitants of Wonderland.

== Trivia ==

* During a croquet game, the Queen issued execution orders at a rate of approximately one per minute, demonstrating pronounced volatility in her responses to game disturbances.
* The Queen maintained a hedgehog as playing apparatus in her croquet games.
* She demonstrated readiness to order executions for minor infractions; she ordered the Hatter's beheading when he sang "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star," which she deemed "murdering the time."
